title: INFWAD – Mix (30 willekeurige vragen)
description:
30 willekeurige vragen uit beide toetsen, net als het echte tentamen: 8 HTML/CSS/JS, 14 Vue en 8 Express. Nodig voor een 5,5: 20 van de 30 goed.

Wil je een nieuwe trekking? Draai `python nieuwe-mix.py` in de map Toetsen/ en klik in Dino op Importeren > Map Toetsen/ > Map nu opnieuw inlezen.

questions.title: Fundamentals 4 – JavaScript
questions.text: According to the lessons, what are the two things a frontend framework like Vue or React does for you?
questions.explanation: You declare what the screen should look like for the data; the framework does the DOM updates.

options.text: It writes your CSS and it hosts your website
It replaces HTML with JavaScript and it compiles your code to C#
It stores your data in a database and handles user logins
It lets you describe the UI as a function of state, and it updates the DOM efficiently when the state changes

questions.title: Vue 1 – Reactivity & components
questions.text: What is `@click` in Vue?
questions.explanation: `@` is shorthand for `v-on:`, and `:` is shorthand for `v-bind:`.

options.text: A shorthand for `v-bind:click`, used to bind a value
A CSS selector for clicked elements
A shorthand for `v-on:click`, used to listen for the click event
A decorator that makes a function reactive

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text:
What does the `?` mean in this interface?
```ts
interface Product {
  id: number
  name: string
  image?: string
}
```
questions.explanation: Optional properties keep existing objects (without an image) valid.

options.text: `image` may be `null` but must be present
`image` is optional: a product can have it but doesn't have to
`image` is a private property
`image` is computed automatically

questions.title: Vue 2 – v-model, computed & composables
questions.text: What does the `.number` modifier do in `<input v-model.number="price" type="number">`?
questions.explanation: Input values are strings by default; `.number` converts them.

options.text: It only allows the user to type digits
It rounds the value to a whole number
It converts the input value to a number before it is stored in the ref
It formats the value as a price

questions.title: Express 1 – Basics
questions.text: Why are the packages `@types/node` and `@types/express` necessary?
questions.explanation: TypeScript doesn't know what's inside Node or Express by default. The `@types` packages only describe them.

options.text: They compile TypeScript into JavaScript
They provide type definitions so TypeScript understands the libraries
They contain the compiled runtime JavaScript logic required to execute Node and Express modules inside a TypeScript environment
They contain the actual source code for Node and Express

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC & EJS
questions.text: What is the difference between `<% %>` and `<%= %>` in EJS?
questions.explanation: Use `<% products.forEach(...) %>` for the loop and `<%= product.name %>` to show a value.

options.text: `<% %>` outputs a value; `<%= %>` runs code without output
`<% %>` is for comments, `<%= %>` is for variables
There is no difference
`<% %>` runs JavaScript without output (loops, conditions); `<%= %>` outputs a value into the HTML

questions.title: Fundamentals 2 – CSS
questions.text: What does `padding: 16px 24px;` mean?
questions.explanation: Two values: top/bottom, then left/right. Four values go clockwise from the top.

options.text: 16px on the left and right, 24px on the top and bottom
16px on the top, 24px on the bottom
16px on the top and bottom, 24px on the left and right
16px of padding and 24px of margin

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC & EJS
questions.explanation: The body has to be parsed first. HTML forms send `urlencoded` data; the built-in middleware turns it into an object.

options.text: `app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }))` before the routers
`res.send()` at the end of the handler
`method="get"` on the form
`import body from 'express'`

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC & EJS
questions.text: What is the difference between `res.sendFile(...)` and `res.render(...)`?
questions.explanation: With EJS set as view engine, `res.render('products', { products })` fills the template on the server.

options.text: `sendFile` is for JSON, `render` is for images
`sendFile` sends a static file as-is; `render` processes a template with data and sends the resulting HTML
`render` sends the file to another server
There is no difference, `render` is the newer name

questions.title: Fundamentals 2 – CSS
questions.text: Where should almost all of the CSS of a real project live?
questions.explanation: Separate stylesheets keep structure and styling apart. `<style>` blocks are for small examples and prototypes, inline styles should be avoided.

options.text: In `style` attributes on each element
In a `<style>` block at the bottom of the `<body>`
In JavaScript, using `element.style`
In separate `.css` files, linked with a `<link>` tag

questions.title: Fundamentals 3 – CSS layout
questions.text: Which CSS centres a child both horizontally and vertically inside its parent?
questions.explanation: With flexbox, `justify-content` centres on the main axis and `align-items` on the cross axis.

options.text: `.parent { text-align: center; vertical-align: middle; }`
`.child { margin: center; }`
`.parent { display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; }`
`.parent { display: grid; grid-template-columns: center; }`

questions.title: Fundamentals 4 – JavaScript
questions.text: What is the difference between a multi-page application and a single-page application (SPA)?
questions.explanation: An SPA fetches only the data it needs and updates the page in place, while the URL and back button still work.

options.text: In an SPA the browser loads one HTML page and JavaScript updates the DOM on navigation; in a multi-page application the server sends a full new page on every click
An SPA has only one page of content; a multi-page application has several
A multi-page application needs a framework, an SPA does not
An SPA can't change the URL in the address bar

questions.title: Fundamentals 1 – HTML & DOM
questions.text: When should you use an `<a>` element instead of a `<button>`?
questions.explanation: Use `<a>` for navigation and `<button>` for actions (save, delete, open a menu).

options.text: When the element has to look like a link instead of a button
When the action should work without JavaScript
When the element contains an icon instead of text
When clicking it navigates to another page or location

questions.title: Vue 1 – Reactivity & components
questions.text: What is the difference between `v-if` and `v-show`?
questions.explanation: `v-show` keeps the element in the DOM and does not support `v-else`.

options.text: `v-if` hides the element with CSS; `v-show` removes it from the DOM
`v-if` only works on components; `v-show` only works on HTML elements
There is no difference, `v-show` is the old name
`v-if` adds/removes the element from the DOM; `v-show` always renders it and toggles `display: none`

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC & EJS
questions.text: In MVC, what is the **model** responsible for?
questions.explanation: For example a `Product` class with `addProduct` and `getAllProducts`.

options.text: The layout and styling of the page
The data and the rules for creating, reading, updating and deleting it
Receiving HTTP requests
Starting the server

questions.title: Vue 4 – Parent/child communication
questions.text: Why does the lesson use `import type { Product } from '../types/Product'`?
questions.explanation: The interface is defined once in `src/types/Product.ts` and imported as a type wherever it is needed.

options.text: Only a type is imported, so it is used by TypeScript and doesn't end up in the JavaScript
`import type` makes the import load faster at runtime
It converts the interface into a class
It makes the Product interface reactive

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs first (A, C), then the promise callbacks. The first callback only *returns* `console.log` without calling it, so B is never logged. Then D.

options.text: A, D, C
A, B, C, D
A, C, D
A, C, B, D

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle hooks & watchers
questions.text:
```ts
// <script setup>
console.log('A')
onMounted(() => console.log('B'))
console.log('C')
```
In which order are the messages logged?
questions.explanation: Code in `<script setup>` runs immediately when the component is created. `onMounted` waits until the component is rendered.

options.text: A, B, C
B, A, C
C, A, B
A, C, B

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text: You see "blocked by CORS policy" in the console when fetching from an external API. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: CORS is decided by the server's response headers.

options.text: Your Vue code has a syntax error
You forgot `await` before `fetch`
The API returned invalid JSON
The server doesn't allow requests from browser JavaScript on your origin; it is a server-side restriction you can't fix from frontend code

questions.title: Express 2 – MVC & EJS
questions.text:
```ts
const price = req.body.price
const withShipping = price + 10
```
For a submitted price of 5, `withShipping` is `'510'`. Why?
questions.explanation: Form values arrive as strings (`{ price: '5' }`). Convert with `Number(...)` first.

options.text: Express adds the numbers as text by mistake
`req.body` multiplies numbers by 100
The `urlencoded` parser converts numbers to arrays
All values in a submitted form are strings, so `+` concatenates them

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.text: In which three states can a Promise be?
questions.explanation: Pending = still running, fulfilled = finished with a value, rejected = failed with an error.

options.text: Loading, success, error
Pending, fulfilled, rejected
Created, mounted, unmounted
Waiting, running, done

questions.title: Vue 6 – Fetching data
questions.explanation: Every page that depends on async data must start loading it, and the lookup must be reactive because the data arrives later.

options.text: Use `router.push` instead of `useRoute`
Start loading the data on this page too (`initProducts()` in `onMounted`) and make the lookup a `computed`, so it updates when the data arrives
Use `v-show` instead of `v-if` for the not-found message
Add `{ deep: true }` to the route

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle hooks & watchers
questions.text: Why should an event listener that is added in `onMounted` be removed in `onUnmounted`?
questions.explanation: Every resource you allocate (listeners, timers, connections) you should clean up.

options.text: Otherwise the listener keeps running after the component is gone, causing a memory leak and bugs
Because Vue throws an error when a component has more than one listener
Because listeners are automatically duplicated on every render
Because `onUnmounted` is the only place where `removeEventListener` is allowed

questions.title: Fundamentals 4 – JavaScript
questions.text: What is logged by `console.log("5" + 3)`?
questions.explanation: With `+` and a string, JavaScript concatenates: `"53"`. This kind of weirdness is one reason the course uses TypeScript.

options.text: `NaN`
An error, because you can't add a string and a number

questions.title: Vue 3 – Lifecycle hooks & watchers
questions.text: Several pages call `useProducts()`. The `products` ref is declared **outside** the `useProducts()` function, at the top of the module. What is the effect?
questions.explanation: A module-level ref is created once and shared by every call. (Bigger apps use a state management library like Pinia for this.)

options.text: All pages share the same products state
Every page gets its own copy of the products
The ref is no longer reactive
TypeScript gives an error because refs must be inside a function

questions.title: Express 1 – Basics
questions.text: How does using a separate "Router" in the Express backend contribute to the "Separation of Concerns" principle?
questions.explanation: Instead of one huge `index.ts`, routes are grouped per area in their own files (`home.routes.ts`, `product.routes.ts`).

options.text: It separates the TypeScript code from the JavaScript code
It separates the logic of the server from the logic of the client
It separates the middleware from the route handlers
It separates the different functional areas (e.g., home vs. products) of the backend into manageable modules

questions.title: Vue 1 – Reactivity & components
questions.text:
```vue
<ProductCard name="product.name" price="product.price" />
```
What does `ProductCard` receive?
questions.explanation: Without `:` the prop is a static string. Use `:name="product.name"` to pass the value.

options.text: The name and price of the product
Nothing, props must always be passed with `v-model`
An error, because props can't be strings
The literal strings `"product.name"` and `"product.price"`

questions.title: Fundamentals 3 – CSS layout
questions.text:
```css
nav { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }
```
With the default `flex-direction: row`, what does `align-items: center` do?
questions.explanation: `justify-content` works on the main axis (horizontal in a row), `align-items` works on the cross axis (vertical in a row).

options.text: It centres the items vertically (on the cross axis)
It centres the items horizontally
It puts equal space between the items
It centres the text inside each item

questions.title: Express 1 – Basics
questions.text:
```html
<form action="" method="post"> ... </form>
```
```ts
router.get('/add-product', showAddProductPage)
```
Submitting the form shows the 404 page. Why?
questions.explanation: Add `router.post('/add-product', ...)` to handle the submitted form.

options.text: There is only a route for GET; the form sends a POST, which no route handles, so it ends up at the 404 handler
The form needs `action="/add-product"` to work
Forms can't be used with Express
The 404 handler catches all POST requests

questions.title: Vue 5 – Client-side routing
questions.text:
```ts
// main.ts
const app = createApp(App)
app.mount('#app')
app.use(router)
```
What goes wrong?
questions.explanation: The order is `createApp` → `app.use(router)` → `app.mount()`.

options.text: The router is registered after the app is already mounted, so routing doesn't initialise correctly
Nothing, the order doesn't matter
`app.use` can only be used for CSS plugins
The app is mounted twice
